events.note: Faint, wide, slow CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the SW in STEREO A COR2. The source is clearly far-sided via CME triangulation, and may only be observed in GOES SUVI 284 as slow moving field lines over the SE limb starting as early as 2026-08-08T15:00Z the previous day; noting this observation as more speculative.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

events.note: CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely on or very near the NE limb, observed as a filament eruption and field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193/304 starting around 2026-08-09T02:52Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on triangulation between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

events.note: Narrow CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. Not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source can be seen as moving field lines beyond the NE limb best seen in SDO AIA 193 imagery starting around 2026-08-09T22:24Z. This eruption may be associated with an active region around N10E105 seen in Solar Orbiter EUI 174 imagery at 2026-08-09T12:06Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on potential source location.

events.note: CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is visible in SOHO LASCO C2 until 2026-08-10T07:00Z and is not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 in real-time due to a data gap in the DSN. The source may be an eruption seen near N10W130 in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery starting at 2026-08-10T01:25Z as brightening and moving field lines.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source location as well as the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

events.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. The source is an eruption and C2.4 flare starting around 2026-08-10T12:30Z from former Active Region 14498, which was located at an approximate longitude of 102 degrees around the time of the eruption, as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the western limb in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195/284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the longitude of former Active Region 14498 based on the approximate rate of solar rotation.

events.note: Faint CME observed to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 only, either too faint or blocked by the pylon in LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely far-sided, observed only in SDO AIA 171 as field line movement over the NNW limb around 2026-08-11T12:43Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

events.note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

events.note: CME first seen to the NW by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-08-012T08:23Z, as well as to the North by GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not seen in SOHO LASCO in real-time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-12T04:35Z. The source of this event is likely far sided, and is seen as field lines opening along or just beyond the West limb (approx. N15W157) in STEREO A EUVI 195 and from beyond the North limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-08-23T07:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

events.note: CME first seen to the East in STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-08-14T05:09Z, as well as by GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME was not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-14T04:48Z. The source of this event is a filament eruption centered at approx. S10E20 with liftoff beginning at approx. 2026-08-14T04:00Z. This filament is heavily deflected to the West as it erupts as seen in SDO AIA, STEREO A EUVI and GOES SUVI 304. Field line opening, dimming and post eruptive arcades are also visible in SDO AIA 171, 193, STEREO A EUVI 195 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

events.note: CME first seen as a halo to the SE by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-08-14T07:38Z, as well as by GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME was not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-14T04:48Z. The source of this event is a C4.1 flare from Active Region 14503 (S17W57) seen peaking at 2026-08-14T07:01Z in SDO AIA 131. Field line opening, dimming and post eruptive arcades are also visible in SDO AIA 94, 171, 193, STEREO A EUVI 195 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

events.note: CME observed to the W in STEREO A COR2 and as a NE partial halo in GOES CCOR-1, not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to DSN gap, but imagery became available with later backfill. The source is far-sided, only likely visible as field line movement over the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 starting as early as 2026-08-14T10:42Z and over the NE limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting around 2026-08-14T10:55Z. This CME is preceded by a faint front that is quickly overtaken by the main bulk of this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: UPDATED BULK measurement based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
SHOCK measurement based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
PRELIMINARY measurement based on triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

events.note: CME first seen to the W in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-08-14T18:23Z. It is also seen to the W in GOES CCOR-1. In real time, this CME is covered by a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source of this CME is most likely related to moving field lines seen beyond the W limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-08-14T17:18Z. An eruption that may be related can been seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 near former AR 14505 (located approximately N15W145) beginning around 2026-08-14T16:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

events.note: CME first seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-08-14T22:24Z. It is also seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C3 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The majority of the CME is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. A possible source is a small filament eruption beyond the N limb best seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2026-08-14T21:52Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

events.note: This CME is visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2 imagery and to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery before a real-time data gap starting around 2026-08-15T04:24Z. This CME is not yet visible in SOHO LASCO C3 due to the aforementioned data gap. In GOES CCOR-1, there is an Earth-shine imaging artifact preventing from seeing the CME initially, but is likely seen to the NE following the imaging artifact. There is no clear source for this CME, but it is believed to be far sided. This CME follows in the same path of the CME first seen in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery starting at 2026-08-14T22:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is a more narrow feature ahead of the front tracked in SOHO LASCO C2 which may adjust the associated longitude by +/- 10 degrees.

events.note: CME first seen to the ENE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-08-15T06:48Z. It is also seen to the ENE in SOHO LASCO C3, and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The source may be related to some fluctuation in filament structures seen near the E limb in SDO AIA 304 for several hours before and after the CME start time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. CME is very slow to start, so the triangulated measurement is based on later frames.

events.note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-08-15T07:24Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NNW in STEREO A COR2. There is no good source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided. This is consistent with measurements.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

events.note: CME first seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-08-15T11:36Z. It is also seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C3 but is not seen in STEREO A COR2 and is mostly obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. There is no definitive source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided. This feature partially overlaps with CME: 2026-08-15T07:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to single perspective and lack of source candidate.

events.note: CME first seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-08-15T13:48Z. It is also seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NNW in STEREO A COR2. There is no definitive source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided. This is consistent with measurement.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.
